Do not create separate pools for ordinary internal roles unless the description treats them as independent communicating participants.
Use data input and output associations between data and activities. Data associations do not define execution order.
Use transaction, ad-hoc or compensation behavior only when its specific semantics are explicitly described.

args.text: When naming BPMN activities, use labels that faithfully preserve the action and its meaning as stated in the process description; do not change or obscure who performs the action.

trace.reason: Check whether an error-driven guideline already covers faithful activity-label wording.

result.rule: When the description distinguishes an event or activity by its action, actor, object, recipient, or another meaningful qualifier: Label each BPMN element so that it preserves those stated details without substituting a broader or different meaning.

When the description distinguishes a process trigger, an activity, or an outcome from other stages of the process: Label each BPMN element according to the meaning of its corresponding described trigger, activity, or outcome; do not substitute a different stage or its purpose or result.

When the description gives an activity together with contextual or explanatory details that are not needed to distinguish the activity in its process context: Label the BPMN task with its core action and necessary object, omitting redundant contextual modifiers while preserving details essential to the activity’s meaning.

When the description identifies an activity by its action and object, or distinguishes it from neighboring activities: Label the BPMN activity with the action and object supported by the description; do not substitute an inferred action or fold a neighboring activity into its label.
